chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, among the obligatory rights of the believer is that his invitation (for a meal) be answered.
ai.seo_question: What is the religious ruling on answering a Muslim's invitation for a meal?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the specific act of accepting a meal invitation to the broader category of obligatory rights (haqq al-muslim) within Shia jurisprudence. This elevates the social interaction from mere etiquette to a religious duty, emphasizing that fulfilling the believer's request strengthens communal ties and reflects spiritual responsiveness, as the Imam notes that such prayers are answered.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar, from Al Moala Bin Khunays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that:
‘From the rights of the Obligations of the Believers is that you answer his invitation (for a meal)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar from Mu‘alla’ ibn Khunayth who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is of obligatory rights of a believer that you accept his invitation.’”
